name: Accordion

fills, never by dividers (R5.8). Use for secondary detail (advanced settings, raw data),
not for primary navigation.

name: ActionBar
description:
The entity header's actions (R12.1): the top-priority actions as buttons, the primary
right-most, the rest under "More actions ▾". It adapts to its container, not the
viewport: as the space narrows, buttons move into the More menu (lowest priority
first), More becomes ⋯, and at the narrowest everything collapses into a single ⋯
menu (R21.2). The bar is right-aligned and one control tall at every level, so the
primary never moves and nothing around it shifts.

props.description:
The room the bar may use, when its container decides it: an entity header, where the
name and facts keep their width first. The bar then folds buttons into More to fit and
is only as wide as what it shows, so the room it leaves stays with its neighbours.
Omitted, the bar measures its own box and asks for room for every button.

name: ConversationLog
description:
The conversation: a scrolling log on a centred reading column, with the composer floating
over its bottom edge.

Column    a reading column (--reading-column) centred in the log, the convention every chat
          follows (R5.4). Wide blocks (tables, charts, code, images) break out wider,
          centred on the text, up to --reading-column-wide and never past the log. Spare
          width is for the context panel beside the log, never for longer lines.
Composer  floats over the transcript in glass-overlay, a small gap from the bottom, on the
          column. The log runs the full height behind it; its end is padded by the
          composer's measured height, so the last message scrolls clear of it, and growing
          the composer never moves what you read (if you were at the end, you stay there).
Asks      pending asks are pinned in the ask dock directly above the composer (R13.8); the
          transcript holds a marker at the ask's place. "Scroll to end" floats above both
          while you are not at the end.
Landing   with `landing` set, the hero, composer and suggestions sit in the middle. The first
          message clears it and the same composer (focus, caret, attachments intact) moves
          to the bottom with a FLIP transition on --duration-slower; instant with motion off.
Pinning   while the reader is at the bottom, new content keeps the bottom in view, so
          streaming text, folding asks and arriving results move what is above, never the
          newest lines. Scrolled up, nothing moves: the pill says "New messages" (R9.4).
A11y      role="log" without per-token chatter: completed answers are announced through
          one polite live region; the scroller is keyboard scrollable (R20.6).

error states that keep the table's box, and opt-in row reordering by drag or keyboard
(`reorder`) that leaves the order to the host.
signature: <T extends RowData>(props: DataTableProps<T>): import("react").JSX.Element

props.name: actions
props.description:
The entity's actions (R12). The row ⋯ menu, the right-click menu and the bulk bar are
the shared action renderers reading this one definition, so they match ActionMenu,
ActionContextMenu and every other surface.

props.name: cardBreakpoint
props.description: Below this width (rem) rows become cards (default 36).

props.name: className
props.description: Classes applied to the outer element for layout. Use the component props and theme tokens for its appearance.

props.name: columns
props.description: Typed column definitions, including rendering, sorting, priorities and filters.

props.name: cursor
props.description: Switch the pager to cursor mode.

props.name: defaultHiddenColumns
props.description:
Column ids initially folded into row/card details. Saved user choices take
precedence, including an explicitly empty hidden list. Reset columns restores
these defaults. Columns with hideable=false remain visible.

props.name: defaultState
props.description: Initial uncontrolled view state.

props.name: density
props.description: Row density for this table. Uncontrolled tables persist the user's choice.

props.name: emptyAction
props.description: The primary action for the unfiltered empty state ("Add a row").

props.name: emptyMessage
props.description:
One line for an empty result with nothing searched or filtered (R2.5), e.g. "No rows
yet". While searching or filtering the table says so itself, with the `noun` (`No rows
match "q3" and 2 filters`), and offers Clear search and Clear filters instead.

props.name: error
props.description: Shown in the body box with Retry. A string should say what failed and what to do.

props.name: filterToggles
props.description:
On/off filters that are not a column ("Show hidden"): rows in the Filters menu, and a
chip while on. Clear filters turns them off too.

props.name: getRowActions
props.description:
Per-row ActionSets, for rows of different kinds (a device list: an endpoint's set is not a
printer's). It replaces `actions`. One row's ⋯ and right-click resolve its own set, so
they match its header exactly. A selection of several kinds (right-click inside it, the
bulk bar) offers the actions every kind's set resolves, bulk in each, and each kind runs
its own definition against its own rows (`resolveRowActions`). Keep the sets stable: the
same object for every row of a kind.

props.name: getRowId
props.description: Returns a stable row identifier for selection, live updates and preferences.

props.name: getRowLabel
props.description:
Accessible label for a row ("NST-C106"): selection, actions and the reorder grip and
announcements use it. Defaults to the first column's text.

props.name: grouping
props.description:
Group the rows (server-side, docs/data-filters.md §7): a header row per group with its
count from the server, which collapses (click, Enter or Space; ← and → on the header;
Alt-click toggles every group). Each expanded group shows its first `pageSize` rows and
a "Show more" line while the server has more; the pager gives way to a count. The
collapsed groups and "Show more" counts are the `groups` state slice (in the URL with
`useTableUrlState({ grouped: true })`). Pass `rows` in group order: each expanded
group's loaded rows, as `groupOf` assigns them.

props.name: height
props.description: "fill" (default) fills a parent with a definite height and scrolls inside.

props.name: id
props.description: Stable id: persists column widths, hidden columns, pins and density per user.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the grid, e.g. "Endpoints".

props.name: live
props.description: Live data: flash changed cells and hold new rows behind an "N new" pill.

props.name: loading
props.description: First load: skeleton rows in the final shape.

props.name: locale
props.description:
BCP 47 locale for this table's numbers, dates, counts and local sorting. Default: the
nearest `LocaleProvider`, then `configureLocale()`, then `<html lang>`, then en-US.

props.name: noun
props.description: Noun for counts in the status bar ("1,284 endpoints").

props.name: onAction
props.type: ((action: ResolvedAction<T>, targets: readonly T[], surface: ActionSurface) => void) | undefined
props.description:
Run actions yourself. By default every surface uses the shared runner: confirm in an
AlertDialog, run, then report with a toast (R12.4, R12.5). With `onAction`, the
confirmation and the feedback are the caller's.

props.name: onDensityChange
props.description: Called with the density the person picks. Pair with `density` to control it; without `density` the table also stores the choice in its preferences.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Called with no arguments when the person presses Retry in the error state; the button shows only when this is set.

props.name: onRowOpen
props.description: Enter or double-click on a row.

props.name: onStateChange
props.description: Called with the next full state and the slice that changed.

props.name: pageSizes
props.description: Page-size choices offered by pagination.

props.name: queryKey
props.description:
Identity of the query behind `rows` (scope, view, anything outside the table's state).
When it changes the rows are a new result; when it does not, changed rows are live
updates and flash. Sorting, the search, filters and the page are part of it already.

props.name: refetching
props.description: A refetch is in flight: rows stay, a thin line runs under the header.

props.name: renderBulkActions
props.description: Replace the bulk bar's action buttons.

props.name: renderRowActions
props.description: Replace the ⋯ menu for a row (render your own trigger, e.g. a shared ActionMenu).

props.name: renderRowContextMenu
props.description:
Replace the context menu's content for a row (or the selection it belongs to). It is
placed inside the shared ContextMenu popup, so build it from Menu parts.

props.name: reorder
props.description:
Row reordering by drag and keyboard (opt-in): a grip column before the checkboxes, also in
cards. The host owns the order and receives each move; see `DataTableReorder`.

props.name: rowCount
props.description: Total rows on the server (offset pagination).

props.name: rows
props.description: The current page of rows, already sorted and paged by the server.

props.name: rowWrapper
props.description: Wrap each row element (e.g. in the shared ActionContextMenu). Must render `children`.

props.name: search
props.description:
The toolbar search (R16.8): a field at the start of the toolbar, beside Filters, that
matches these identifying fields on the server. Its query is the `search` state slice
(`q` in the URL with useTableUrlState). Typing waits 220 ms, then returns to the first
page. `/` focuses it while the table has focus. On a narrow toolbar it is an icon
button that opens the field, and an active query shows as a "Search: …" chip.

props.name: selectable
props.description: Show checkboxes and allow selection (default true).

props.name: state
props.description: Controlled slices. A slice left out is owned by the table.

props.name: status
props.description: Extra status bar content (connection state, last sync).

props.name: toolbar
props.description: The table's own controls (a view switch, Refresh), at the end of the toolbar.

props.name: updatedAt
props.description: When the data was last refreshed (status bar: "Updated 2 min ago").

name: EntitySettingsDialog
description:
Every entity's Settings dialog (R12.6, glass-ux-components-plan §5.1): an `lg` dialog whose
header is the entity's identity tile with "Settings" and a data subtitle, an L3 tab rail,
and Cancel / Save. One form spans every tab, so Save sends one document.

- A tab with unsaved changes shows a neutral dot; after a refused save, tabs with errors
  show a danger dot, the dialog opens the first of them and focuses the field.
- Server errors (`SettingsSaveError.fieldErrors`) appear at their fields and clear as the
  field changes.
- Save is disabled until something changes, then confirms in place (R15.10). Changes to
  privileged fields (reassignment, credentials, routing) make it "Verify and save": a
  step-up first, then the save.
- A save refused because someone else saved first (SettingsConflictError) keeps the
  edits and says so beside Save, with Reload.
- Closing with unsaved changes asks first (R13.7). Cancel reverts and closes.
- On phones it is a bottom sheet; the rail becomes chips, or a picker past six tabs.
signature: ({ open, onOpenChange, form, tabs, tab, defaultTab, onTabChange, media, title, subtitle, entityName, onSaveError, onSaved, footerStart, size, preview, loading, saveDisabledReason, privileged, onVerify, onReload, }: EntitySettingsDialogProps): import("react").JSX.Element

the box it is given (width AND height), so it fits a table cell, a header, a tile and a pane:

  micro    height < 5rem or width < 10rem: label, value, delta and an inline sparkline in one row

(state), `Trigger`, `Popup` (positioned, with an optional title and close button),

- `unmount`: Ends the closing phase of the popover after an externally controlled closing animation finishes.
Call `preventUnmountOnClose()` in `onOpenChange` first, otherwise the popover completes closing on its own.
Whether it leaves the DOM is decided by `keepMounted` on the portal.
- `close`: Closes the popover imperatively when called.

props.name: modal
props.description:
Determines if the popover enters a modal state when open.
- `true`: user interaction is limited to the popover: document page scroll is locked, and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled.
- `false`: user interaction with the rest of the document is allowed.
- `'trap-focus'`: focus is trapped inside the popover, but document page scroll is not locked and pointer interactions outside of it remain enabled.

On touch devices, a `true` modal blocks outside taps but leaves the page scrollable unless the popup spans nearly the full viewport width, matching native iOS behavior.

When `modal` is `true`, focus trapping is enabled only if `<Popover.Close>` is rendered
inside `<Popover.Popup>`. It can be visually hidden with your own CSS if needed, such as
Tailwind's `sr-only` utility.

When `modal` is `'trap-focus'`, render `<Popover.Close>` inside `<Popover.Popup>` so touch
screen readers can escape the popup.

is opened by touch — then the popup itself is focused to avoid opening the virtual keyboard.

- `true`: Move focus based on the default behavior (first tabbable element or popup).
- `RefObject`: Move focus to the ref element.
- `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`).
  Return an element to focus, `true` to use the default behavior, `null` to fall back to the default behavior, or `false`/`undefined` to do nothing.

name: Tree
description:
The navigation tree (a sidebar's records grouped by owner). Groups collapse; leaf rows
are fa-item rows, two lines with a description, with an optional status dot on the icon. Keyboard: ↑ ↓ move,
→ opens or enters a group, ← closes or returns to the parent, Home / End, Enter selects
(toggles a group), and typing jumps to the next matching name. One row is tabbable (roving
tabindex). Rows are virtualised, so thousands of rows cost only the rows on screen.

name: Treemap
description:
Nested rectangles sized by value — SpaceMonger/WinDirStat for disk usage. Tiles are soft
tints of their branch's (or kind's) colour with the 2px surface gap between them; labels
appear only where they fit and truncate with an ellipsis, the size line only where there is
height for it. Click or Enter drills into a tile; the path, Backspace and Escape go back.

  compact  one level of tiles with labels, passive
  full     two levels (groups with a header, their children inside), the drill path, the
           tooltip (size, share of parent and of the whole) and keyboard navigation by
           direction

props.name: compact

props.name: leading
props.description: Extra controls before the standard ones (the phone window switcher).

props.description: Whether the window fills its available workspace.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called when the person presses Close; run close guards before removing the window. The button is shown only when this is supplied.

props.name: onMinimise
props.description: Called when the person presses Minimise. The button is shown only when this is supplied.

props.name: onPopOut
props.description: Called when the person presses Pop out. The button is shown only when this is supplied and not `compact`.

props.name: onReturn
props.description: Popped-out windows offer "Return to workspace" in place of pop-out.

props.name: onToggleMaximise
props.description: Called when the person presses Maximise or Restore (per `maximised`). The button is shown only when this is supplied and not `compact`.

props.description: The heading or title content.

name: WindowManagerProvider
description:
Provide a window manager to the tree and connect it (load the persisted layout, join
cross-tab sync) before the first paint after hydration.
signature: ({ manager, children }: { manager: WindowManager; children: ReactNode; }): import("react").JSX.Element

props.name: children
props.description: The content or component slots rendered inside the component.

props.name: manager
props.description: The store from `createWindowManager`. Create it once (module scope or a ref); a new instance reconnects.

name: WindowScopeChip
description:
The scope chip in a window's app bar: the organisation's avatar and name, shown only when
the window belongs to a scope other than the current one. Narrow windows keep the avatar,
and the tooltip names it. Part of the app bar's drag surface, like the title.
signature: ({ scope }: { scope: string | null; }): import("react").JSX.Element | null

props.name: scope
props.description: The window's scope id (`WindowEntry.scope`), or null for an unscoped window, which shows no chip.

name: WindowScopeProvider
description: Supplies the current scope and how to draw a scope to the window layer's scope chips and dock groups. A null or undefined `value` turns scope labelling off.
signature: ({ value, children }: { value: WindowScopes | null | undefined; children: ReactNode; }): import("react").JSX.Element

props.name: children
props.description: The content or component slots rendered inside the component.

props.name: value
props.description: The controlled value. Keep it in application state and update it in the change callback.

name: WindowSwitcher
description: Phones: every open window in a bottom sheet, plus the routed view.
signature: ({ open, onOpenChange, primaryLabel, }: { open: boolean; onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void; primaryLabel?: string; }): import("react").JSX.Element

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the next open state when the sheet is dismissed (swipe, Esc, scrim) and with false after the person chooses a window. Pair with `open`.

props.name: open
props.description: Controls whether the overlay is open.

props.name: primaryLabel
props.description: Visible label for the primary action.

name: Workspace
description:
The windowed workspace: the routed `primary` view plus every open window from the
enclosing `WindowManagerProvider`, tiled, floating or maximised, with the dock. On phones
the focused window covers the screen and a switcher lists the rest. Reports its size to the
manager so new windows are placed inside it.
signature: ({ primary, primaryLabel, dock, scopes, className, }: WorkspaceProps): import("react").JSX.Element

props.name: className
props.description: Classes applied to the outer element for layout. Use the component props and theme tokens for its appearance.

props.name: dock
props.description: Show the dock of open windows (default true).

props.name: primary
props.description: The routed view. Render EntityHeader, WindowFrame.Body and WindowFrame.StatusBar.

props.name: primaryLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the primary window, normally the entity or page title.

props.name: scopes
props.description:
The tenant scope the user is in and how to draw one (R14.4). Windows from another scope
show its chip in their app bar, and the dock groups windows by scope. Omit for a
product without scopes.
